## Goal
`_hardened` (`src/freemyid/wizard/server.py:209-215`) sets the CSP (45-46), `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, but no test asserts any of them on the wizard (the only CSP test is for the website). The bad-Host branch (174-176) returns a plain `Response` without `_hardened`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. For every GET route in `app.routes` (path parameters faked, authenticated session), the response carries all five headers with their exact values; the CSP equals `server.CSP`, includes `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `script-src 'self'`, and has no `unsafe-inline` or `unsafe-eval`.
2. The same holds for: the unauthenticated 403 (183-186), the CSRF-refused 403 (203-206), the 303 redirect after a valid POST, a file under `/static`, and a 404.
3. The bad-Host 403 (174-176): assert the headers; if they are missing, strict xfail citing `server.py:176` as a finding.
4. No HTML response body contains the session token, and no response sets any cookie other than `freemyid_session` (44).

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
